title: JavaScript Design Patterns Core Check
description: Check your understanding of common JavaScript design patterns, their purposes, tradeoffs, and when to use them.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: A reusable solution shape for a common programming problem
A JavaScript syntax rule enforced by the browser
A package that must be installed from npm

questions.explanation: A design pattern is a reusable way to think about and solve a common design problem.

questions.prompt: What is a good reason to use a design pattern?

options.text: It solves a real problem such as duplication, coupling, or complex object creation
It makes code look more advanced
It removes the need for clear names

questions.explanation: Patterns are useful when they improve real code structure, not when they add ceremony.

questions.prompt: What does the module pattern help with?

options.text: Grouping related code and exposing a small public API
Forcing all code to be asynchronous

questions.explanation: Modules organize related code and keep unexported details private to the module.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the factory pattern?
questions.explanation: A factory creates objects in one place, often applying defaults, validation, or implementation selection.

questions.prompt: What is a major caution with the singleton pattern?

options.text: It can introduce hidden shared state that is hard to test or debug
It can only be used with arrays
It always creates a new instance

questions.explanation: Singletons are convenient but shared mutable state can make behavior harder to trace.

questions.prompt: What does the observer pattern allow?

options.text: Many listeners can react when a subject changes
One function can only run once
All errors can be ignored safely

questions.explanation: Observers subscribe to a subject and are notified when something happens.

questions.prompt: What is the strategy pattern best for?

options.text: Choosing between interchangeable algorithms or behaviors

questions.explanation: Strategies let code select one behavior from a family of compatible behaviors.

options.text: Converts one interface or data shape into another expected shape

questions.explanation: Adapters help incompatible interfaces work together by translating between shapes.

questions.prompt: What is the goal of a facade?

options.text: Provide a simpler interface over complex code
Make an object impossible to import

questions.explanation: A facade hides complex steps behind a clearer public operation.

questions.prompt: What does a decorator or wrapper usually do?

options.text: Adds behavior around existing code while preserving its interface

questions.explanation: Wrappers commonly add logging, timing, validation, retries, or caching around existing behavior.

questions.prompt: When is the command pattern useful?

options.text: When actions need to be stored, queued, logged, retried, or undone
When a value must never be passed as an argument
When there is only one local variable

questions.explanation: Commands represent actions as values, which makes action management possible.

questions.prompt: What JavaScript feature is central to the iterator pattern?
questions.explanation: JavaScript uses the iterable protocol, `Symbol.iterator`, iterators, and `for...of` for iteration.

options.text: Passing required services into code instead of hard-coding or importing them directly
Adding random dependencies to every function

questions.explanation: Dependency injection makes dependencies visible and easier to replace in tests or different environments.

questions.prompt: What does composition over inheritance generally recommend?

options.text: Build behavior by combining focused pieces unless inheritance clearly fits
Always create the deepest possible class hierarchy
Store all behavior in one global object

questions.explanation: Composition often gives JavaScript code flexible combinations of behavior without rigid class trees.
